dialogue.opening_line: It hurts more than I expected, but I don't want anything that will knock me out.

action_responses.check_identity: Of course. I'm Eleanor Shaw, and the details on my wristband are correct.
action_responses.assess_pain: It is about seven out of ten. It aches all the time and catches sharply when I try to move.
action_responses.check_allergies_and_prescription: Mrs Shaw watches while you check the simulated records.
action_responses.explain_analgesia: I was worried it might make me too sleepy when my daughter visits. If that concern is covered, I would consider it.
action_responses.seek_consent: Yes, I understand what you have explained and I would like to accept it.
action_responses.administer_charted_option: Thank you. I hope it makes moving a little easier.
action_responses.reassess_pain: It is nearer four now. It still hurts when I move, but it is more manageable.

fallback_responses: Can you explain what the next step would be?
I want to be involved in the decision.

facts.fact: Her current pain is 7 out of 10 and is worse on movement.
She is worried that stronger pain relief could make her too sleepy for her daughter's visit.
After a clear explanation that addresses her concern, she has chosen to accept the charted option.
After the authored reassessment interval, her pain is 4 out of 10 and more manageable.

seek_consent: ask if she wants pain relief

dialogue.opening_line: They said I might go home today. I think I've understood everything.

action_responses.create_privacy: Thank you. I didn't want everyone passing by to hear this.
action_responses.seek_discussion_permission: Yes, we can talk about it now.
action_responses.explore_concerns: I'm most worried about it leaking when I'm out. I keep saying I'm fine, but I don't really know what I would do.
action_responses.explain_in_chunks: That was easier to follow when we took one part at a time.
action_responses.use_teach_back: I can explain the routine part, but I'm not sure who I should contact if something goes wrong.
action_responses.seek_family_permission: Yes, I would like my sister to join us for the final review.
action_responses.arrange_specialist_review: That would reassure me before I go home.

fallback_responses: Could we take that slowly? I don't want to pretend I understand.
Aisha listens, then glances at the folded leaflet.

facts.fact: She is worried about leakage when outside the house but may initially say she is fine.
She can describe routine care but is unsure whom to contact if a problem occurs.
She has chosen to involve her sister in the final review.

cases.title: Personal care, accessible communication and withdrawn consent

patient.dialogue_style: Direct and friendly when he can hear; becomes quiet if rushed
nonverbal_palette: Mr Chen tilts his better ear towards the learner and watches their face closely.

dialogue.opening_line: Sorry, I didn't catch that—the television is quite loud.

action_responses.reduce_noise: That's much better. I can hear you when you face me like that.
action_responses.check_hearing_support: Yes please—the left hearing aid feels loose.
action_responses.create_privacy: Thank you for closing the door.
action_responses.check_preferences: I can wash my face and upper body myself. I only need help lower down.
action_responses.seek_consent: Yes, I agree to that amount of help.
action_responses.start_agreed_care: All right, I'm ready to begin.
action_responses.pause_on_withdrawal: Thank you for stopping. The water feels too cold; I need a moment.

fallback_responses: Please face me when you speak so I can follow you.
Mr Chen waits for the background noise to settle before replying.

facts.fact: He wants to wash his face and upper body independently and needs help only with lower-body washing.
He can hear more clearly when the speaker faces him and the background noise is reduced.
He has withdrawn consent because the water feels too cold and wants care to pause.
